sections.h2: Where is Bridgewater, Massachusetts, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Bridgewater sits in Plymouth County about 25 miles south of Boston and roughly 35 miles east of Providence. It covers 28.2 square miles, which makes it one of the larger municipalities in the county by land area.

The town borders West Bridgewater, East Bridgewater, Halifax, Middleborough and Raynham, and Brockton is about five miles to the north. The Taunton River runs through it, and Lake Nippenicket lies along the western edge. A large part of the Hockomock Swamp Wildlife Management Area is in the western part of town, so some house lots back onto wetland or conservation land.

Wikipedia lists these named neighborhoods and villages:

  • Stanley
  • Scotland Park
  • Pratt Town
  • Paper Mill Village
  • South Bridgewater

Two ZIP codes serve the town, 02324 and 02325. If you are selling a house here, the neighborhood name matters less to a buyer than the street, the lot and how close it is to Route 24, Route 18 or the train.

sections.h2: How does Bridgewater work as a town and a city at once?
sections.html:
Bridgewater is officially the Town of Bridgewater, but it runs under a city form of government. Voters approved the change in an April 24, 2010 town election, which replaced the Board of Selectmen and open Town Meeting with a nine-member Town Council.

The council has three district councilors and six councilors at large, and the Town Manager, Assessor and Tax Collector are appointed. For a seller, the practical point is that permits, tax questions and municipal records go through town offices at the center of town, and the assessor's page on bridgewaterma.gov is the place to confirm anything about your bill.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Bridgewater's housing and economy?
sections.html:
Bridgewater was set up as a township from Duxbury on June 3, 1656, and it was placed in Plymouth County when counties were formed in 1685. Over the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries its economy leaned on factories, including iron works, paper mills, sawmills and a boot and shoe factory.

The Bridgewater Iron Works is a registered historic site, and most of the factory was torn down in 1994 and turned into Ironworks Park. The old boot and shoe factory building stood off Broad Street next to the commuter rail tracks.

By the late 1960s the local economy depended heavily on state institutions: the Old Colony Correctional Center and other Massachusetts correctional facilities, Bridgewater State Hospital and the teachers' college that is now Bridgewater State University. The Department of Correction still operates several facilities in the Bridgewater Correctional Complex.

sections.h2: How do you get around Bridgewater, and who commutes from it?
sections.html:
Bridgewater has both highway and rail access. Interstate 495 crosses Route 24 in the southwestern corner, with only a one-mile stretch of the interstate inside town limits.

  • Routes 18, 28 and 104 meet at the Town Common in the center of town.
  • Route 104 runs east to west and has ramp access to Route 24.
  • The MBTA Commuter Rail Fall River/New Bedford Line stops at Bridgewater station on the Bridgewater State University campus.
  • The nearest commercial air service is at T. F. Green Airport near Providence and Logan International Airport in Boston.

Buyers who commute to Boston, Brockton or Providence will look at how close a house is to Route 24 and the station. Mention both in a listing or in any conversation with a buyer.

sections.h2: How do Bridgewater State University and the schools affect sellers?
sections.html:
Bridgewater State University was founded in 1840 as a normal school, and Wikipedia reports about 8,000 undergraduate and 1,500 graduate students as of 2022.

Public school students attend the Bridgewater-Raynham Regional School District. George H. Mitchell Elementary serves kindergarten through grade two, M.G. Williams Intermediate serves grades three to five, Bridgewater Middle School serves grades six to eight, and Bridgewater-Raynham Regional High School is west of the town center.

High school students may also choose West Bridgewater Middle-Senior High, Bristol-Plymouth Regional Technical School, Coyle-Cassidy High School, Cardinal Spellman High School, Norfolk County Agricultural High School or Bristol County Agricultural High School.

sections.h2: What does New England weather mean for a Bridgewater house?
sections.html:
Snow load is the weather risk with a documented local example. In February 2015 the roof of Mitchell Elementary collapsed under heavy snow, and students were moved to other school buildings.

A private owner can face a smaller version of the same problem, so a buyer's inspector may look closely at the roof. Brockton, five miles away, records about 34 inches of snow in an average year according to NOAA normals reproduced on Wikipedia, so Bridgewater owners should expect similar winters.

The Taunton River and the Hockomock Swamp also mean wet ground in parts of town. If your lot is near water, expect a buyer to ask about basement moisture, sump pumps and flood history. You can answer those questions from your own records, and your insurer can tell you about coverage.

sections.h2: How do Bridgewater property tax bills work when you sell?
sections.html:
Bridgewater bills real estate tax four times a year. The town has used quarterly billing since July 1, 2010.

  • Preliminary bills go out at the end of June and are estimates without a tax rate or assessed value. They are due the first business day of August and November.
  • Actual bills are mailed at the end of December and show the rate, the assessment, abatements, exemptions and previous payments. They are due the first business day of February and May.

The state approves the tax rate, usually in December. If you sell in the middle of a fiscal year, ask your closing attorney how the current quarter is handled and whether the bill is paid at the table. The assessor's online database shows the property record card for your address.

sections.h2: What rules apply when you sell a house in Bridgewater?
sections.html:
Two statewide rules come up on almost every sale. First, the deed excise tax is $2.00 for each $500 of price or fraction of $500, under Massachusetts General Laws chapter 64D, section 1, and the statute exempts instruments where the state, a town or the United States is a party. The registry of deeds collects it when the deed is recorded.

Second, the Department of Fire Services says you need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the sale requirements. Call the Bridgewater fire department as soon as you have a closing date, because the department charges a fee and schedules the inspection. Battery alarms older than ten years or expired must be replaced with ten-year sealed photoelectric alarms that have a hush feature.

The Mass.gov alarm page explains how to date your alarms and which standard applies to your house.

sections.h2: How can you sell a house fast in Bridgewater?
sections.html:
You have three routes: list it, sell it yourself or take a direct cash offer. A listing usually works best on a house in good shape. A cash sale makes more sense when the house needs work, has tenants, is part of an estate, or you need a closing date you control.

Before you choose, gather the deed, your latest tax bill, any permit records, and a list of known repairs. If the house is inherited, bring the probate paperwork. If tenants live there, bring the leases. Cash Home Buyers can look at a Bridgewater house as it stands, without cleaning or repairs, and you can compare what we put in writing with a listing estimate before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is Bridgewater, MA in?
faqs.a: Bridgewater is in Plymouth County, Massachusetts. Brockton, the largest city in the county, is about five miles to the north.

faqs.q: When are Bridgewater real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Preliminary bills are due the first business day of August and November, and actual bills are due the first business day of February and May, according to the town's assessing page. Confirm the exact dates on your bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke detector inspection to sell in Bridgewater?
faqs.a: Yes. Massachusetts requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for the sale or transfer of a home. Call the fire department once you have a closing date, since it charges a fee.

faqs.q: How much is the Massachusetts deed excise tax?
faqs.a: It is $2.00 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of $500, per MGL c. 64D, s. 1. Barnstable County has a lower rate of $1.50, which does not apply to Bridgewater.

faqs.q: Is Bridgewater a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both in practice. Its official name is the Town of Bridgewater, but it has had a city form of government with a Town Council since the 2010 vote.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Bridgewater that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. You can list it as is, sell to an investor, or take a cash offer. Buyers will price in the repairs they find, so gather your permits and repair history first.
